title: SAFEGUARDS Act of 2026
official_title: To amend title 49, United States Code, to establish funds for investments in aviation security, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: House passage recorded July 13, 2026 per the latest action. Sponsored by a Republican member with six cosponsors and referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security. The measure now moves to the Senate.
summary: Amends title 49, United States Code, to dedicate portions of the 9/11 Security Fee (collected under section 44940) to two aviation security funds beginning in fiscal year 2027. Under subsection (h) of section 44923 as amended, the first $500M in fees each fiscal year is deposited in the existing Aviation Security Capital Fund and the TSA Administrator is directed to impose the fee so as to collect at least $500M for that fund. A new subsection (i) creates the Aviation Security Checkpoint Technology Fund (ASCT Fund) into which the next $250M in fees is deposited each fiscal year — available until expended for testing, procurement, deployment, installation, and sustainment of aviation security checkpoint technology, again with a fee-setting instruction to collect not less than $250M. A sense of Congress declares that the 9/11 Security Fee is airline-passenger-paid and should be used exclusively for aviation security, and that diversion should end no later than 2027. A conforming amendment updates the cross-reference in section 44940(j)(1) from "section 44923(h)" to "subsections (h) and (i) of section 44923."
brief: Dedicates the first $500M of the 9/11 Security Fee each fiscal year to the Aviation Security Capital Fund and creates a new Aviation Security Checkpoint Technology Fund that receives the next $250M, both starting in fiscal year 2027.

top_lines.headline: $500M to the Aviation Security Capital Fund
subs: Beginning FY2027 and each fiscal year thereafter, the first $500M from 9/11 Security Fee receipts is deposited in the Aviation Security Capital Fund
TSA Administrator directed to set the fee so as to collect at least $500M annually
Amounts available to the Administrator to make grants or enter related agreements under section 44923

top_lines.headline: New Aviation Security Checkpoint Technology Fund
subs: Beginning FY2027 and each fiscal year thereafter, the next $250M in fees (after the $500M Capital Fund deposit) is deposited in the ASCT Fund
TSA Administrator directed to set the fee so as to collect not less than $250M annually
Amounts available until expended for testing, procurement, deployment, installation, and sustainment of aviation security checkpoint technology

top_lines.headline: Sense of Congress
subs: 9/11 Security Fee is an airline-passenger-paid fee established to sustain aviation security
Revenue should be used exclusively for aviation security (screening, technology upgrades, personnel support)
Use of the fee for unrelated purposes undermines public trust
Diversion of fee revenue should end no later than 2027, per section 44940(i)(4) of title 49, U.S.C., as in effect on the date of enactment

top_lines.headline: Conforming Cross-Reference
subs: Section 44940(j)(1) reference updated from "section 44923(h)" to "subsections (h) and (i) of section 44923"

items.main: Names the Act the "Spending Aviation Fees for Equipment, Guaranteeing Upgraded and Advanced Risk Detection and Safety Act of 2026" or the "SAFEGUARDS Act of 2026."
items.detail: Short-title section only; no substantive effect.

items.main: States that the 9/11 Security Fee (49 U.S.C. 44940) is an airline-passenger-paid fee established with the express purpose of sustaining aviation security; that revenue should be used exclusively to fund activities, programs, equipment, and initiatives directly improving commercial aviation security (including passenger and baggage screening, security technology upgrades, and personnel support); that use for unrelated purposes undermines public trust; and that diversion should be ended no later than 2027 in accordance with section 44940(i)(4) as it read on the date of enactment.
items.detail: Sense-of-Congress declarations are non-binding but frame the operative amendments in section 3.

items.main: Amends subsection (h) of section 44923 of title 49, U.S.C., so that beginning FY2027 and for each fiscal year thereafter, the first $500M derived from fees received under section 44940(a)(1) is available to be deposited in the Aviation Security Capital Fund, and the TSA Administrator is directed to impose the fee so as to collect at least $500M annually for that Fund.
items.detail: Strikes the second, third, and fourth sentences of paragraph (1) of subsection (h) and inserts the new $500M-floor sentences. Paragraphs (2) and (3) are struck and replaced with a single paragraph (2) making Fund amounts available to the TSA Administrator for grants and related agreements under section 44923.

items.main: Establishes the Aviation Security Checkpoint Technology (ASCT) Fund within DHS. Beginning FY2027 and each fiscal year thereafter, after the first $500M is deposited into the Aviation Security Capital Fund, the next $250M from fees received under section 44940(a)(1) is available to be deposited in the ASCT Fund; the Administrator must set the fee so as to collect not less than $250M annually for the ASCT Fund. Amounts are available until expended for testing, procurement, deployment, installation, and sustainment of aviation security checkpoint technology.
items.detail: Adds new subsection (i) to section 44923 (redesignating the existing subsection (i) as (j)). ASCT Fund disbursement authority mirrors the Capital Fund's — available to the TSA Administrator to make grants or enter related agreements.

items.main: Conforming amendment: paragraph (1) of section 44940(j) (as redesignated) is amended by striking "section 44923(h)" and inserting "subsections (h) and (i) of section 44923."
items.detail: Updates the 9/11 Security Fee statute's cross-reference to reflect that the fee now flows into both the Capital Fund and the new ASCT Fund.

gaps: The bill does not identify what happens to 9/11 Security Fee receipts above the combined $750M ($500M + $250M) floors — the current allocation to general revenues or other uses is not described within this Act's text.
The bill does not define "aviation security checkpoint technology" for the ASCT Fund beyond authorizing testing, procurement, deployment, installation, and sustainment.
The bill does not specify grant-application procedures, matching requirements, or eligibility criteria for either fund.
The bill does not include an oversight or reporting requirement on how deposited amounts are spent.

added: $500M annual floor from 9/11 Security Fee to Aviation Security Capital Fund starting FY2027
New Aviation Security Checkpoint Technology Fund receiving the next $250M annually starting FY2027
New fee-setting directives requiring TSA to collect at least $500M for Capital Fund and not less than $250M for ASCT Fund
Sense of Congress that the 9/11 Security Fee should be used exclusively for aviation security and that diversion should end no later than 2027
modified: 49 U.S.C. 44923(h) restructured: prior second, third, and fourth sentences of paragraph (1) replaced; paragraphs (2) and (3) replaced with a single disbursement-authority paragraph
49 U.S.C. 44940(j)(1) cross-reference updated to point to both subsections (h) and (i) of section 44923
removed: Second, third, and fourth sentences of prior 49 U.S.C. 44923(h)(1)
